    • ABSOLUTE_ERROR

      private static final double ABSOLUTE_ERROR
      Maximum allowed difference between the estimator and the in-test reference implementation of Kinematics_ECEF.m. Both perform the same arithmetic in a different order of operations, so they only differ by floating point rounding: the largest difference observed over 2000 seeded pairs of frames per pass is 2.0e-14 (time interval of 0.02 s) and 7.6e-15 (time interval of 1 s). 1e-9 leaves margin for rounding while being three orders of magnitude below the smallest algorithmic error fixed in the estimator (7.8e-7 m/s^2).
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • COMPARE_SPECIFIC_FORCE_ERROR

      private static final double COMPARE_SPECIFIC_FORCE_ERROR
      Maximum allowed difference in specific force, expressed in meters per squared second, between the ECEF, ECI and NED kinematics estimators. It is the smallest power of ten satisfied by the three algorithms over the seeded, kinematically consistent pairs of frames of the comparison test, where the largest observed differences are 9.9e-4 (ECEF vs. NED), 1.0e-3 (ECI vs. NED) and 2.9e-5 (ECI vs. ECEF).
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • COMPARE_ANGULAR_RATE_ERROR

      private static final double COMPARE_ANGULAR_RATE_ERROR
      Maximum allowed difference in angular rate, expressed in radians per second, between the ECEF, ECI and NED kinematics estimators. It is the smallest power of ten satisfied by the three algorithms over the seeded, kinematically consistent pairs of frames of the comparison test, where the largest observed difference is 1.5e-9 (both ECEF vs. NED and ECI vs. NED).

    • ROUND_TRIP_ERROR

      private static final double ROUND_TRIP_ERROR
      Maximum allowed difference between the kinematics fed to ECEFInertialNavigator and the kinematics recovered by ECEFKinematicsEstimator from the navigated frame. Navigator and estimator implement exactly inverse equations (Groves eq. (5.73)-(5.85) and (5.36)), so the only expected difference is floating point rounding: a rounding of about 1e-16 relative in velocities of about 4e2 m/s divided by a time interval of 0.1 s gives about 1e-12 m/s^2, hence 1e-9 leaves three orders of magnitude of margin while remaining far below the smallest algorithmic error this test must detect (7.8e-7 m/s^2).
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • MIN_POSITION_SENSITIVITY

      private static final double MIN_POSITION_SENSITIVITY
      Minimum difference in specific force, expressed in meters per squared second, that must be observed when gravity is evaluated at the end instead of at the start of the round trip long time interval. Positions are about 36 m apart and the gravity gradient is about 3e-6 s^-2 vertically and 1.5e-6 s^-2 horizontally, which yields a difference of about 1e-4 m/s^2; 1e-6 is two orders of magnitude below that and three orders of magnitude above ROUND_TRIP_ERROR.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values
